card.name: Inside romanized Chinese names
card.fires_on: Pieces partway through romanized Chinese (pinyin) names, usually the start of a later syllable such as x, sh, Ch or hu. Seen in person names, book titles and herbal formula names.

modes.label: Person names
modes.description: A later syllable inside a pinyin personal name.
modes.example: Lin<< Ch>>ao — applied an electric current

modes.label: Herbal formula names
modes.description: A syllable partway through a pinyin herbal formula name.
modes.example: (ji sheng<< sh>>en qi wan) treats musculoskeletal

card.writes: It favors further pieces of Chinese-style names and syllables, such as '儿', '央' and '尺'.
card.plain: It marks the middle of a Chinese name written in English letters, where another syllable is expected next.
